text:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to finalize the launch ingredients for the regional routing rollout. TL;DR: staged feature flag, canary cohorts, A/B quality checks, and a one-button kill-switch. Who owns what?

Devon: I can own the flag Ops (naming, rollout steps, kill-switch endpoint). propose name: `routing-regional-v3`. :+1:

Ajay: Canaries: start at 3% NA for 1h, then 15% NA+EU for 3h, then 40% global for 12h. If metrics are green we continue. If not, immediate rollback to previous variant.

Corey: For Dedicated customers we should add an opt-out allowlist — don't auto-apply to any reserved pools. Also add an enterprise override flow so account teams can opt certain customers into the new routing early.

Maya: Agreed on opt-out. Also need launch gates: latency, error-rate, cost delta, and quality. Draft thresholds below — please sanity-check:
- 99p latency increase < 25ms
- error rate delta < 0.05% absolute
- per-token cost delta < 8%
- eval-suite quality drop < 0.5 (MRT metric)

Lex: +1 on eval-suite. We'll run A/B on a seeded production-like eval set (1000 prompts) during the canary window. If quality regresses > 0.5 we abort. I’ll own the eval run and post results in the thread.

Devon: Flag config snippet (ops format):
```yaml
flag: routing-regional-v3
phases:
  - pct: 3
    regions: [NA]
    duration: 3600  # seconds
  - pct: 15
    regions: [NA,EU]
    duration: 10800
  - pct: 40
    regions: [global]
    duration: 43200
kill_switch: /ops/flags/routing-regional-v3/disable
metrics: [p99_latency, error_rate, token_cost, eval_quality]
```

Devon: Kill switch command (for runbook):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.redwood.internal/flags/routing-regional-v3/disable" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"reason":"emergency rollback - perf/quality"}'
```

sre-bot: Deploy-check: infra capacity check passed for NA/EU regions. Auto-scaling headroom = 22%. Alert thresholds preset for p95/p99 spike rules.

Corey: One more ask: synthetic warmup traffic for 10 minutes at 5qps to prime KV cache and embeddings cache. Add to preflight and mark as mandatory.

Ajay: Add real-customer holdback: top-20 paying customers should be manually held back unless their CSM approves opt-in. We can't risk regressions for big accounts.

Maya: Owners/next steps:
- Devon: implement flag & kill-switch (ETA: EOD tomorrow)
- Lex: run A/B eval during 3% and 15% windows, post runbook check results (ETA: start with canary)
- Ajay: orchestration of phased rollout + synthetic warmup (ETA: formal runbook by tomorrow morning)
- Corey: enterprise allowlist flow + CSM opt-in process (ETA: two days)
- SRE: monitor dashboards + set alert runbooks (ETA: today)

Devon: naming/CID note: use `routing-regional-v3` across code, flagstore, and console. I'll add ACL so only ops can flip full-global.

Lex: one more metric suggestion — add a simple semantic drift check (BLEU-ish on common prompts) during canary. If drift > threshold, abort.

Maya: Good call. Add to gate list: semantic_drift < 0.6.

Corey: Heads-up for support: prepare canned reply for customers if they see temporary latency spikes — short blurb + link to status page. I'll draft.

Ajay: Also recommend a 30-minute dark-launch where we shadow traffic to new path but respond with old results, just to validate instrumentation. Low overhead, high confidence.

Maya: Love it. Add dark-launch step before 3% canary in the runbook. Final question: do we want automatic progressive increases (flag-controlled) or manual increases after human signoff?

Devon: Auto-increase with automated gates is fine, but require manual approval to go beyond 40% or to enable for Dedicated pools. So hybrid.

sre-bot: Note: automated rollback action configured for any of these triggers: p99 spike > 40ms, error rate increase > 0.1%, semantic_drift > 0.6, eval_quality drop > 0.5.

Maya: OK — agreed. I'll update the launch checklist and post a final runbook link when ready. If no objections, we'll proceed with the plan and target a mid-week low-traffic window next week. :eyes:

Corey: :thumbsup:

Devon: :rocket:

Lex: I'll queue the eval and add the semantic drift test to the dashboard.

Ajay: I'll draft the runbook now and ping for review.

Maya: Thanks all — I'll add these owners to the product rollout card and tag you for sign-offs.
